newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-JORDAN SCORES 50 AS BULLS BEAT HEAT.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-JORDAN SCORES 50 AS BULLS BEAT HEAT.

text.p: Michael Jordan scored 50 points and Dennis Rodman grabbed a season-high 22 rebounds as the Chicago Bulls remained unbeaten with a 106-100 victory over the Miami Heat Wednesday.
Jordan had double figures in all four quarters. The eight-time scoring champion, who has scored 50 points against 18 different teams, scored 56 in a playoff game at Miami in 1992.

"The scenario tonight was perfect for a competitor," Jordan said. "The club missed a lot of opportunities but I was in my rhythm. I don't have to score 50 points every night for us to win but we didn't get the normal support from our bench."
Rodman, who has won five straight rebounding titles, has pulled down 41 rebounds in his last two games.
"I get paid to take the bumps and grinds every night," Rodman said. "When we're down, we never panic, we just keep on playing."
The Bulls trailed 47-36 with 4:10 to go in the second quarter before Jordan scored nine points in a 20-6 run that closed the period.
Scottie Pippen sank a three-pointer with two seconds left that gave Chicago a 54-53 lead. Jordan then stole the inbounds pass and made another three-pointer at the buzzer.
Pippen scored 17 points for Chicago (4-0), which won its first five games last season en route to a record 72 wins and an NBA championship.
In Charlotte, 7-footer Matt Geiger had 22 points including a career-high four three-pointers as the Hornets dealt the Los Angeles Lakers their first loss of the season, 88-78.
Geiger, who entered the game 8-for-27 from three-point range in his four-year career, fuelled a third-quarter run that gave the Hornets the lead for good. He also had 10 rebounds.
Anthony Mason scored 19 points for the Hornets (2-1), who allowed just 11 points in the fourth quarter.
Charlotte won without injured guards Glen Rice and Muggsy Bogues.

Shaquille O'Neal had a season-low 22 points and 10 boards, Eddie Jones scored 16 points and Nick Van Exel added 15 for the Lakers (3-1), who were coming off an impressive road win over the New York Knicks the previous night.
"We started out wanting to control the tempo and not have a running game, which is what the Lakers have been doing," Hornets coach Dave Cowens said.
"It is hard to play a back-to-back game like Los Angeles did tonight. They were fatigued and came in thinking they had an easy win. Sometimes, it is all in your mind."
In Boston, Dino Radja had 23 points and 11 rebounds and David Wesley added 19 points as the Celtics overcame a 23-point halftime deficit to beat the Indiana Pacers 94-84.
Boston outscored the Pacers 38-8 in the third quarter. Eric Williams poured in 16 points and Radja had 13 over the decisive 12 minutes.

"That was a great feeling today in the third quarter, playing defence," said Radja. "I knew someone would cover for me and I was there for others. This is an Indiana team, this isn't like Vancouver or somebody. This is a team which played in the (Eastern Conference) finals."
"You see what happens when you play good defence?" Celtics forward Rick Fox said.
Reggie Miller scored 28 points for Indiana, which set franchise record lows with just eight points in a quarter and 26 in a half.
At Detroit, Joe Dumars scored 18 points and Otis Thorpe chipped in 17 and 13 rebounds as the Pistons improved to 4-0 with a 103-84 victory over the Dallas Mavericks.
Detroit played without star forward Grant Hill, who is nursing a sore right wrist. Hs listed as day-to-day.
Dallas (1-3) has dropped three straight.
At Washington, Chris Webber scored 22 points and grabbed a career-high 21 rebounds to lead the Bullets to a 96-86 triumph over the San Antonio Spurs.
Juwan Howard had 22 points and 12 rebounds for the Bullets (2-1).

Sean Elliott had 18 for the Spurs (1-3), who were just 2-of-15 from three-point range but scored more than 80 points for the first time this season. San Antonio again played without injured All-Star centre David Robinson.
In Milwaukee, Vin Baker scored 20 points and grabbed 11 rebounds and rookie Ray Allen added 20 points as the Bucks cruised to a 105-89 rout over the winless Vancouver Grizzlies.
The Bucks (3-0) are off to their best start since going 7-0 in 1971, when they were coming off their only NBA championship.
Rookie Shareef Abdur-Rahim and Blue Edwards had 18 points each for the struggling Grizzlies (0-4), who have lost their first four games by a combined 78 points.
